card.name: Kpanlogo
card.tagline: Ga recreational drum-dance of post-independence Accra youth
card.profile: Kpanlogo is a recreational dance and music form originating in the early 1960s among urban Ga youth in Accra, Ghana, now performed nationwide (Wikipedia). Its music draws on older Ga traditions - gome, oge and kolomashie - using the nono (metal bell), fao (gourd rattle) and a set of kpanlogo drums in 'male', 'female' and 'master' roles. The main bell pattern matches the Cuban son clave. Credited to Otoo Lincoln, who set an Ansee folktale about three princesses to a new beat, it was briefly restricted as 'indecent' before Kwame Nkrumah approved a revised choreography in 1965 (Ghana Goods; ThisWorldMusic).
card.insight: Ghanaian master drummer C.K. Ladzekpo described Kpanlogo as 'an urban youth dance drumming and a symbol of commitment' by young people shaping post-colonial Africa's future (GhanaRemembers).
